summary.text: 米 is a whole-graph picture of scattered grain. Its early referent was probably dehusked grain broadly; it commonly means rice today. The central stroke’s identity is disputed.

formation.text: Pictographic: the graph depicts scattered grain as a whole. Interpretations of its central stroke include a sieve or a grain stalk, but that detail is not needed for the overall grain-picture reading.

history.text: Early forms are described as small marks above and below a central stroke. The marks later lengthened and joined into a cross-like form; Chu examples show that joining had begun before small seal script. Forms are also recorded in bronze inscriptions, small seal script, and the Shuowen entry, but the evidence does not establish a complete graphic sequence. The selected oracle-bone-style image is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact.
The Shuowen entry glosses 米 as grain seed and interprets its form as depicting grain from a plant. This is a lexicographic interpretation, not independent confirmation of the graph’s origin.

uncertainties.text: The central stroke may represent a sieve, a grain stalk, or a non-specific separator; its identity remains unresolved, though the overall grain-picture analysis does not depend on it.
The precise dates and contexts of reported early uses are unresolved, as is the chronology by which the broad grain sense became commonly rice-specific.

senses.text: 米 is reported in oracle-bone use for rice or grain. Scholarly discussion identifies its early referent as probably dehusked grain broadly, rather than a single crop; the precise first-use date and inscription context are unresolved.
米 commonly means rice in modern usage.

In Japanese, 米 is used for the length unit metre following the use of 米突 to render French mètre by sound. This is a separate word use, unrelated in meaning to grain. The exact route by which 米 alone became current is unresolved.

developments.text: The broad early grain sense is commonly specialized to rice in modern usage, though when this change occurred is unresolved.

limitations.text: 米’s Japanese use for ‘metre’ is a graph borrowing: 米突 rendered French mètre by sound, after which 米 came to be used on its own. This does not show a semantic development from grain to a length unit; the date and precise route are unresolved.

Other reported early uses include writing 敉 ‘pacify’, a sacrificial name, and clan names. Their inscription contexts and relationship, if any, to the grain meaning are unresolved, so they are not treated as semantic developments or separate senses.
Other Japanese readings are listed, but their senses and histories are not explained here; only the metre use is supported by the cited account.

overview.text: 米 pictures scattered grain, probably grain kernels with their husks removed. It commonly means rice today.

items.period: Shang dynasty script style (modern redraw; not a dated specimen)
items.caption: In this modern redraw of an oracle-bone-style 米, short marks sit above and below a long diagonal stroke. The scattered arrangement fits the grain-pictograph explanation; the diagonal’s identity remains disputed.
items.alt: Black marks with a long diagonal stroke running from lower left to upper right, three short strokes above it and two below.
items.selection_reason: The redraw makes the scattered-grain arrangement visible and supports the pictographic account, while the diagonal itself does not settle the competing interpretations.
items.rights: Public domain, as stated on the file description page; modern vector redraw, not an ancient artifact image.

limitations.text: The central diagonal has been interpreted as a sieve or as a grain stalk; its identity is unresolved. This modern redraw shows a script style, not a dated inscription specimen.
